login.title: Sign in
login.body: Enter your email address: a sign-in link is sent right away, valid for fifteen minutes and for one use only. Do you have a password or a passkey? Use the link below the form. As an owner, two-step verification is required at every sign-in.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.body: The first time, scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy…). After that, enter the 6-digit code it shows each time you log in, or tick "Remember this device": you won't be asked for it on this device for 90 days. After 5 wrong codes, two-factor authentication is blocked for 15 minutes.

home.title: Today
home.body: What needs your attention, across all events, sorted by urgency: overdue, today, waiting on someone else (the client or a vendor), then the next fourteen days. “Deal with first” keeps the first seven items, grouped by kind (follow-ups and messages, tasks, payments, decisions and signatures, prospects); each part gives its count and leads to its page (“See in Tasks”, “See payments received”…), each line says who has to act and leads to the action in one click; a task takes the same line as in « Tasks », without the menu: its title opens its panel, the couple's name leads to their event, « Done » ticks it, and « Review them » shows the tasks done today. Below, full width, the calendar: your events, appointments, tasks in the colour of their category and unpaid vendor due dates; “‹”, “Today” and “›” page through it, “Month”, “Week” and “List” change the view, a click on a day shows its detail. On a phone, the current week. Then the remaining items, and your events in progress, with the countdown. “To send”: a relationship message prepared by Symbola (reminder, brief…), to send from your own mailbox; one click opens the “Prepare the email” window.

faq.q: How do I change the follow-up delays for quotes and prospects?
faq.a: In Settings › Prospect follow-ups: by default, a sent quote after 7 days and a silent prospect after 14 days.

faq.q: Where do I resume a tutorial I started?
faq.a: In Tutorials, in the menu: the tutorial in progress comes first, with the whole path.

faq.q: I ticked a task by mistake?
faq.a: An “Undo” message stays for ten seconds after the tick: it restores the task.

faq.q: Where is the calendar?
faq.a: In Events: the calendar of your weekends is there, with the list.

faq.q: How do I quickly create an event, a task, a vendor, a contact, a quote or an expense?
faq.a: With « + Create » at the top of every screen, or the N key outside a field: six entries, each with its own line. The event, the vendor and the contact open their screen; the task, the quote and the expense open a short form without leaving the screen, and the screen's wedding is named (« Task for Léa & Maxime »).

faq.q: How do I make more room on screen?
faq.a: On a computer, “Collapse menu”, at the top of the menu, keeps only its icons: their names show on hover or with the keyboard, and the screen takes the space freed. “Expand menu” brings it back. The choice is kept on this device.

settings.title: Company and VAT
settings.body: Your company record (SIREN, address, legal form, trade) and your VAT regime: they appear on your quotes and invoices. The trade sets the vocabulary and starter templates. Other settings are filed by section in the left menu. Fill in the postal code and city before your first invoice and, if you are VAT-registered, say whether you opted for VAT on an accrual basis. Identity, address and printed contact details are saved together, with “Save company details”.

faq.q: I am moving from the VAT exemption to charging VAT: what do I do?
faq.a: Change the regime here: new quotes and invoices apply the rate; documents already issued do not change.

admin.title: Console overview
admin.body: At a glance: service status, figures across all organisations, what needs action (expired invitations, two-factor authentication not set up, last backup) and activity over the last 6 months. Never an organisation name, amount or content in these figures.

faq.q: Where does the last backup status come from?
faq.a: The nightly backup script reports each run: start, end, result and size. With no success for over 26 hours, the status turns into an alert.

faq.q: What does "active organisation" mean?
faq.a: An organisation where at least one team account has logged in within the last 30 days.

adminSettings.title: Suite settings
adminSettings.body: Regulatory values shared by all organisations, such as the VAT exemption thresholds. Update them when the regulations change. You also choose here which compliance assistant checks planners see.

adminHealth.title: Health
adminHealth.body: Shows whether the application responds and its deployed version, to check the service at a glance.

invitation.title: Creating your account
invitation.body: This invitation link is personal and works only once. Choose your password: you will then set up two-factor authentication.

profile.title: My account and security
profile.body: Your first and last name: your team sees them in “Who’s doing it” and in notifications (never the couple or vendors); each one is saved on its own when you leave the field. Choose the language Symbola uses for you. Your password and two-factor authentication protect your account; "Forget all my devices" asks for the code again on trusted devices. "Sign out all my other devices" closes your other sessions, for example after losing a phone. “My signature”: your name, job title and links at the end of the e-mails you send.

faq.q: How do I change my password?
faq.a: Log out, then use "Forgot password" on the login screen: a link lets you choose a new one.

faq.q: I have a new phone: how do I set up two-factor authentication again?
faq.a: Ask the suite operator to reset it: you will get an email and scan a new QR code at your next login.

faq.q: How do I add someone to my team?
faq.a: Team accounts are created by the suite operator; the person receives a personal invitation by email.

eventsList.title: Event list
eventsList.body: All your prospects and ongoing events; « Finished » keeps those closed or cancelled. « List », « Columns » or « Calendar », always in the same place: the filterable table, options by stage, or the coming months. Below, the workload over the next twelve months; two events on the same day are flagged in both views. Start with « New event » (an ongoing enquiry, or a signed event), or filter the list by name, status, source or year. To try the module safely, start the guided trial below.

faq.q: Where do I find a past event?
faq.a: In "Past", at the top of the list: it keeps completed and lost events, with the same filters.

faq.q: Why is a year missing from the filter?
faq.a: The filter only offers the years in which you have events, plus the current and next year.

faq.q: Does the guided trial leave anything behind?
faq.a: No: the sample wedding is marked as a trial, excluded from statistics and exports, and deleted when the trial ends.

eventsNew.title: Create an event
eventsNew.body: One entry, "New event": first say where it stands — an ongoing enquiry (it stays an Option) or signed, in preparation (it becomes Confirmed and gets the task list of its type if its date is set) — then give it a name. The date, the client and the type are optional or suggested; the venue, the source and a second client are completed from its page. If you already track the event in another tool or a spreadsheet, "Import your files" leads to the import page without creating anything. If the date falls on the same day as another confirmed or optional event, Symbola flags it before saving, without blocking you.

faq.q: What is the difference between an enquiry and a signed event?
faq.a: An enquiry is not signed: the event is an Option. It becomes Confirmed when you change its status on its page's timeline, or when the quote is signed.

faq.q: Where do I enter the source or a second client?
faq.a: On the event page, Couple tab: "Source and clients".

eventsDetail.title: Event page
eventsDetail.body: The whole event, in tabs. The « Summary » opens on the next action and who has to act, then the event's health (planning, budget, client decisions) and the next fourteen days; « Edit the details », at the top of the event profile, opens a panel where they are edited, the event's time zone included. The top timeline shows where it stands: Option, Confirmed, In preparation, Event day, Closed. Click a step to set it; « Event day » applies by itself on the day of the event, and closing is offered from the next day. « Postpone the event… » asks for the new date: once you confirm the postponement, the planning's due dates follow, except tasks already done and those whose date you set by hand; the ones that would fall in the past are listed first. « Cancel the event… » opens a window that says what will happen and asks for a reason: the data stays, links close, reminders and scheduled deposit invoices stop, and a credit note is offered for each issued invoice; « Keep the event » backs out. A cancelled event is restored from its page (« Restore the event »): it goes back to « Option ». The « Event profile » gathers estimated and confirmed guests, venues, contacts, style and notes; venues are managed in the « Day programme » tab (address, town, times, on-site contact), the first being the reception venue. In the same tab, each sequence of the schedule is a line: “Edit” opens it in place, “Add a sequence” creates one; nothing is sent until you click “Save the schedule”, which says how many lines are waiting, and “Discard changes” brings back the saved schedule. The « Tasks » tab shows the event's tasks, « To do » first, with their filters (who's doing it, period, category, state) and « New task », the event already chosen; under the title, the count and the date the planning's due dates are counted from. A task can be given to you, a colleague, the couple or a retained vendor, who ticks it in their space; its attachments, comments and note stay within the team. Its panel shows its « Place in the planning » (how many days before the big day, and whether it is a key step). Ticked by mistake, a task comes back with « Undo » for ten seconds, then with « Reopen task ». The « Next step » banner suggests the next stage (send the quote, apply the planning, create the couple's links). In « Budget and vendors », each row says where the choice stands (« Selected », « 2 being compared », « To find »); « + Add vendors » offers, for each record of the trade in your directory, « Compare » or « Select », never automatically. The item window compares vendors side by side (quote, availability, worked together before, last follow-up, note): « Select », « Set aside », then « Change vendor » or « Unselect », without deleting the line; « Next item » moves on. « Take over the selected vendors (PDF) » reads the vendors export from your previous software: each vendor is found in the directory or created, then selected on the line of their trade, after your check. Each tab has a « Settings » link to its templates. Overlap warnings leave out your clients, who attend every sequence, and are read day by day. PDFs separate the days of a multi-day schedule; the team version puts the internal note under each sequence.

faq.q: How do I mark an event as lost?
faq.a: With the "Mark as lost…" link under the timeline: it asks for the reason, used in your statistics.

faq.q: Why is the planning timeline empty?
faq.a: It starts once the event is confirmed: then apply a template from the Planning timeline tab.

faq.q: The date changes: what happens to the tasks?
faq.a: The app offers to shift the due dates of unfinished tasks; nothing moves without your approval.

faq.q: What does the couple see?
faq.a: What you open to them, through a personal link, with no account or password: their tasks, the schedule, the budget as read-only, never your internal notes. Create their links in the Couple tab; a paying parent can see only some budget categories.

faq.q: How do I share their times with a vendor?
faq.a: In the Couple tab, create a link for a retained vendor: they see the date, the venues, the latest shared version of the schedule (their sequences in full, the day at a glance in titles and times) and your contact details, nothing else (no prices, no budget, no other vendors, no internal notes). Tick “Ask for a code when opening” to have a code sent to their e-mail each time they open it.

faq.q: How do I have the client approve a choice?
faq.a: In the Couple tab, “Client decisions” section: have the client choose between the vendors shown for an item, approve an expense or approve the schedule. The answer is time-stamped and in the person's name; you then retain the vendor or commit the expense in one click. An answered decision is never changed: ask for a new one.

faq.q: How do I move the rest of the programme?
faq.a: In the Programme tab, change an item's start time: the page offers to move the next items by the same amount, start and end, in one click, and "Undo" stays available for ten seconds. When you type, the duration gives the end time, and the other way round; the person in charge is picked from the ones already entered.

faq.q: How do I follow up with a vendor whose contract isn't signed?
faq.a: With « Log a follow-up », in « Today », the summary or the item window: you follow up your usual way, then log how (phone, email, text, in person), when, a note if needed and when to come back to it. Nothing is sent; the template message can be copied if useful. The vendor leaves « Today » until the reminder, and the follow-up goes into the activity feed.

faq.q: How do I file and share the event's documents?
faq.a: In the Documents tab: upload a map or a document into a folder (“Maps”, “Caterer”), upload a new version without losing the earlier ones, and open the preview without downloading anything. Nothing is shared until you tick “With the clients” or “With the vendors”; issued invoices appear on the clients' portal automatically. For someone without a personal link, create a share link for 1 to 30 days: it opens that document only, each opening is logged in the activity feed, and you can revoke it at any time. Quotes, invoices and attachments from other screens appear there too, read-only.

faq.q: How do I share the schedule with clients and vendors?
faq.a: In the Schedule tab, “Share the schedule” freezes a numbered, dated and signed version: clients and vendors read that version, not your changes in progress, and see “New version of the schedule” at the next one. The section says what has changed since the last share; each version stays available to view and print. Internal notes are never shared.

eventsSettings.title: Budget lines
eventsSettings.body: The lines each new event receives (venue, caterer, photographer…). They were prepared for your trade: add, rename, reorder by dragging. A change applies to upcoming events, not to existing ones.

faq.q: Does changing a line affect existing events?
faq.a: No: only new events get the updated list; add the line by hand to an event already created.

faq.q: Where are sources and loss reasons?
faq.a: In Settings › Sources and reasons, just below in the menu.

eventsTemplates.title: Planning timeline templates
eventsTemplates.body: Your typical task lists, placed before or after the event date (D-365, D-30, the day…). “New template” asks for its name then opens it; you can also load the starter template. Click a template to see its tasks: a task is added or edited in the right-hand panel. Linked to an event type, a template applies by itself when a dated event of that type is created, options included (with no template for that type, the first template created); it can also be applied from the Planning tab.

faq.q: Does editing a template change ongoing events?
faq.a: No: a template is copied into the event when you apply it; events already prepared do not change.

eventsProgramTemplates.title: Schedule templates
eventsProgramTemplates.body: Your typical wedding-day schedules, moment by moment. “New template” asks for its name then opens it; click a template to see its lines. A line is added or edited in the right-hand panel, without recreating it. A template is applied from an event's Programme tab; participants named after a budget line are linked to it.

faq.q: Can I download the schedule?
faq.a: Yes, from the event page: as a PDF, couple version (without internal notes) or vendor version.

clientEvent.title: Your space
clientEvent.body: Your organiser has opened this space for you with a personal link, with no account or password. At the top, your next three actions and what you are asked to decide; further down, what they have shared with you: your tasks to tick, the schedule of the day in its latest shared version, the budget in three figures and its instalments, the documents shared with you and your invoices, to open or download. Paid an instalment? Declare it: your organiser will confirm it. This link is for you only: please do not forward it. For a company, you can enter the purchase order number when signing the quote.

vendorSpace.title: Your vendor space
vendorSpace.body: Your organiser has opened this space for you with a personal link, with no account or password. You will find the date, the venues, the schedule they have shared with you (your sequences in full, the day at a glance in titles and times, to download as a PDF with its version number; a new version is flagged to you), the tasks they give you (tick them once done), the documents shared with you and how to reach them. This link is for you only: please do not forward it.

budgetSettings.title: Budget allocation
budgetSettings.body: An allocation splits a total budget across your lines, in percentages adding up to 100 %. Create one to suggest estimated amounts when you simulate an event's budget. It is optional: an event has a budget from the start. The alert threshold (90 % by default) raises an alert when an event's committed spending would exceed that share of its envelope.

faq.q: Do I need one allocation per type of wedding?
faq.a: It helps if your weddings fall into price ranges: create several and choose the right one on each budget.

budgetDetail.title: Event budget
budgetDetail.body: Day-to-day budget follow-up is in the event's “Budget and vendors” tab: per item, planned, actual, variance, paid, left to pay and next instalment; the row unfolds onto its schedule, and “Open” (or a click on the row) opens the item window, in five sections: Vendors, Amounts, Payment schedule, Documents and Item settings. This page keeps the detail. Each event line is a category; it holds lines (“Dinner, 120 guests”, “Drinks reception”…), each with its vendor and five amounts: estimated, quoted, committed (filled in when you retain the vendor), paid, and left to pay, calculated. “Edit” opens a line in place: change its label, vendor, rate and amounts, on as many lines as you like, then “Save the budget” writes them together; “Discard changes” brings back the saved budget. The simulation and its allocation by category fold away once the lines are set; the allocation is saved the same way, with a single “Save the allocation”. Under each line, attach the quote, contract or invoice, and set the instalments (deposit, balance; a percentage applies to the vendor's committed amount): once paid, they make up the line's paid amount, and the next ones show in “Today”. The envelope is the client's wanted budget; above the alert threshold a banner says so, and retaining a vendor asks for confirmation. Amounts are entered including VAT, each line with its VAT rate (20% by default); if the event's quote is for a business client, the amount excluding VAT shows under each amount. “Export to XLSX” or “to PDF” gives the budget and instalments, in your documents' colours.

faq.q: Does the couple see the budget?
faq.a: Yes, read-only in their portal, if their link opens the Budget section: the whole budget, or only the categories you choose (for a paying parent).

faq.q: Where are attached quotes stored?
faq.a: In private storage, after an antivirus check; they open through a temporary link.

faq.q: Why is the amount excluding VAT not shown?
faq.a: It shows for a business client: choose “Business” as the client type on the event's quote. Without a quote, the client is an individual and the budget stays including VAT.

quotesCatalog.title: Services catalogue
quotesCatalog.body: Your reusable services: label, unit, price excl. VAT, VAT rate and category. Add an item at the bottom of the page; it is offered in your quotes right away. Once archived, it is no longer offered but stays on the quotes that use it. State whether the item is a service or goods: the invoice derives the category of the transaction from it. “Edit” opens an item in its row; each change is saved when you leave the field, and “Undo the last change” takes it back.

faq.q: Does changing a price affect quotes already sent?
faq.a: No: the price is copied into the quote when you add the item.

quotesSettings.title: Quotes and invoices
quotesSettings.body: The default validity of your quotes, the numbering series prefixes (quotes, invoices, credit notes, earnest money receipts), your payment terms and the payment methods you accept. Payment terms have two texts: one for individuals and non-professionals, one for business clients, with the late payment penalty rate you choose. Numbers are assigned per year, without gaps. A method you turn off is no longer offered when you record a payment; payments already recorded keep theirs. For a business client, the payment term (within the legal limits) and the discount are printed on the quote and the invoice.

faq.q: Can I keep my current numbering?
faq.a: Yes: choose your series prefix; numbers then follow on, year by year.

faq.q: Which penalty rate should I choose for a business client?
faq.a: Both rates offered are lawful: the ECB rate plus 10 percentage points, or three times the statutory interest rate. Use the one in your usual terms. The penalty sentence and the €40 fixed recovery fee are added automatically to your terms for a business client.

quotesDetail.title: Composing a quote
quotesDetail.body: The quote opens on its lines and totals; tabs hold the rest: proposal page, payment and deposit, buyer and delivery, fees and commissions, contract and signature, then invoices and credit notes. The “Before sending” box, then “Quote follow-up”, gives the state of each section and leads to it. The main button, at the top, is always the next step: send the quote, get it signed, then invoice. Build the quote from the catalogue or free lines (“Edit” opens a line in place); totals update as you go. Plan the deposits, then send it for signature: once signed, an option becomes « Confirmed ». A sent version is frozen; to change it, create a new version. Signers take the name, e-mail and billing address from the contact's record; an address corrected when sending is kept there if the box stays ticked. For a business client, choose the buying company and note its purchase order; a delivery address only if goods are delivered elsewhere. Before each sending, a "Pre-send checks" panel points out what deserves a look, without blocking anything. Every invoice and credit note is a Factur-X: a PDF that also carries the electronic invoice file.

faq.q: How do I invoice a deposit?
faq.a: On the signed quote, issue the deposit invoice for that instalment, then the balance invoice at the end.

faq.q: Can an issued invoice be edited?
faq.a: No, it is final: correct it with a credit note, which keeps numbering gap-free.

faq.q: How do I offer options?
faq.a: Tick "Optional" on a line: it shows with its price, out of the total. Once the quote is sent, the client ticks the options they keep on their portal; the total follows, and the choice locks when signing starts. You can also tick for them (choice made over the phone).

faq.q: Why is sending refused?
faq.a: A required mention is missing: insurance, mediator, general terms, VAT number… The message names each field, with a link to where to fill it in. The list of mentions is to be validated by your chartered accountant.

faq.q: Deposit or earnest money?
faq.a: As soon as there is a payment schedule, the quote must say whether advance payments are deposits or earnest money: their effects differ on cancellation. The chosen word appears on the schedule, the PDF and the invoice.

faq.q: How do I generate the contract?
faq.a: Once the quote is sent, choose a template, how the contract is concluded and the optional clauses, then generate. Whatever prevents it is named: empty variable, clause still to draft, missing legal information, deposit clause that does not match. The generated contract is frozen; a change creates a new version.

faq.q: Does the right of withdrawal apply?
faq.a: It depends on how the contract is concluded (at a distance, off-premises) and on the client (consumer). Symbola applies the rules validated by the lawyer; the exception for services on a fixed date is not offered for a wedding. At a distance, the client orders on their portal before signing; they may ask for the service to start before the end of the period.

faq.q: When is the deposit invoice issued?
faq.a: Automatically once everyone has signed, or the day after the withdrawal period ends if the clients did not ask for an immediate start. If a mention is missing, “To do” says so and you issue it in one click once the field is filled in. Earnest money does not trigger an invoice on its own.

faq.q: What if I ask for earnest money?
faq.a: Earnest money is paid in a single instalment and is not invoiced. When you record its payment, Symbola creates a non-tax receipt in its own series. The balance invoice shows the full price, with the earnest money as a payment.

faq.q: How does the balance deduct deposits?
faq.a: Rate by rate: each deposit invoice, net of its credit notes, is deducted from its own VAT rate, both the net amount and the VAT. Deposits and balance add up exactly to the quote.

quotesPayments.title: Upcoming payments
quotesPayments.body: The year's three figures (signed, invoiced, collected), then the unpaid instalments of your quotes, sorted by date with a monthly total. Mark an instalment paid from its quote. An overdue instalment is flagged « Overdue » and shows up in « Today ».

faq.q: Do guided trials count?
faq.a: No, their instalments never appear here.

quotesEReporting.title: E-reporting
quotesEReporting.body: For your private clients, some invoicing data must be declared on your approved platform (from 1 September 2027). Choose a period, check the totals, then download the export to upload.

faq.q: Do I have to send e-invoices to my couples?
faq.a: No: for private individuals, only the data declaration (e-reporting) is required.

importFile.title: Importing data
importFile.body: Choose what you are bringing over: your contacts (CSV or Excel), your vendors or your event sheets from your current tool, or another file. Each screen (vendors, events, contacts, budget, programme, guests) also has its own “Import” button, set to the right type. As soon as you click, a window shows how the reading is going. Nothing is saved before you confirm, and an import can be undone from its summary.

faq.q: What happens to my file?
faq.a: It is checked by the antivirus and then discarded: only its rows are kept, until the import is finished.

importColumns.title: Recognising columns
importColumns.body: A table shows each column of your file with two examples, what it becomes on the record (a field by its name, “A note on the record” or “Do not import”) and its status: recognised, chosen, ignored or to choose. Columns to choose come first. On the right, the preview shows the first row of the file as a record and follows your choices. An uncertain suggestion is never chosen for you.

importMatches.title: Matching existing records
importMatches.body: When a row looks like a vendor already in your book, the file row and the existing record are shown side by side (name, trade, city, email, phone, number of events), with the differences spelled out. Choose “It's the same”, “These are two vendors” or “Decide later”. If only the first name is shared, the suggestion is “To check” and they stay two vendors unless you say otherwise. Filter “To check”, “New”, “Updates”; “Accept all” confirms the safe suggestions. While a suggested match is waiting for your decision, “Continue” stays on this screen: decide row by row, or all at once with “Accept the suggested matches” or “Create the rows as new”. In a budget, a row without a budget line takes the one from the row above, and the screen says so.

importGaps.title: Gaps report
importGaps.body: Columns with no match are decided at the “Columns” step. Rows that will not be imported are shown at the “Review and confirm” step, with their reason, and can be downloaded as CSV to be corrected.

importConfirm.title: Confirming an import
importConfirm.body: Before importing, the assistant sums up the effects: records created and updated, types and tags created, columns kept as notes on the record, rows rejected, with a preview of the corrected values. The button says what will be imported.

importUndo.title: Import log and undo
importUndo.body: At the end, the summary comes first: created, updated, ignored, columns kept as a note, each one clickable. “Check the N vendors” opens the list filtered on this import. During the undo period, “Undo this import” (folded) names the records edited by hand since, and you choose: undo the import except those records, or undo everything.

privacySearch.title: Personal data
privacySearch.body: Look up everything you hold about a person: enter an email, a phone number or a name (accents and case ignored). The search queries each module then the person's events; a module that does not answer is flagged. To export or erase, record the request: its case guides you.

faq.q: Someone asks for their data: what do I do?
faq.a: Record the request, search for the person, tick their records, then export: you get a readable PDF and a ZIP archive.

faq.q: Someone asks to be forgotten?
faq.a: Tick their records, then request the erasure preview: each record is deleted, anonymised or kept as the law requires.

privacyRequests.title: Requests from individuals
privacyRequests.body: Record each request received (access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection) with its date: its case opens with the one-month legal deadline. It guides you to the reply. A close deadline is flagged in the menu and on the home screen.

privacySettings.title: GDPR settings
privacySettings.body: Retention periods (based on the CNIL guidelines, to be checked by a lawyer) and the alert threshold for requests. They feed the monthly purge list, which you always approve.

privacyExport.title: GDPR exports
privacyExport.body: An export answers an access or portability request: a readable PDF and a ZIP archive, kept in private storage and deleted automatically on the date shown. Your internal notes are included: read the export before sending it.

privacyErasure.title: Erasure request
privacyErasure.body: The preview shows, record by record, what will be deleted, anonymised or kept (invoices 10 years, signed quotes 5 years). Once confirmed, each module does its part. Then download the timestamped proof and send the reply: the request closes once the reply is marked sent.

privacyPurge.title: Monthly purge
privacyPurge.body: Each month the list gathers what has passed its retention period: prospects that went nowhere, finished relationships, documents at the end of retention, names of people in requests closed for longer than the set proof period. Approve it: each row is purged, except those you exclude with a reason. Nothing is purged without you.

allTasks.title: Tasks across all your events
allTasks.body: The tasks of all your events and of your business, in one list: those of an event and those tied to none (VAT, insurance, accounting, "No event"). "New task", at the top, opens a task's panel, with or without an event; without an event, it can repeat, and the next one is created when it is done. Filter by Event, Who's doing it, Period (late, this week, next 15 days, this month, between two dates), Category and State (to do, done, all): each applied filter becomes a chip that "×" removes, and "Clear filters" removes them all. "My tasks" shows yours in one click. The count says how many tasks the list shows out of how many ("4 tasks out of 11 to do · filtered"). "Group by" sorts the list by month, by event or by person: with the "Late" period, you see each person's late tasks, with their count. Each line: the title (a click opens its panel), the event, the due date and its state in words, who's doing it, "Done" and the "⋯" menu ("Change date…", "Assign to…", "Open event", "Delete"). "Select" shows a box on each line and a bar at the bottom of the list: "Done", "Change date…" (shift by N days or all on the same day), "Assign to…", "Category…" and "Delete", each for the ticked tasks, with "Undo" for ten seconds; "Done selecting" or Esc leaves it. A task ticked by mistake is found with "State: Done", most recent first, with who ticked it and when, and "Reopen". An imported event with no tasks is flagged at the top, with a way to bring in its list. On a phone, "Filters" opens the filters at the bottom of the screen. "Calendar" places the same tasks on their due date, month by month, with the same filters.

faq.q: Do the couple's tasks appear here?
faq.a: Yes: they are marked "for the couple", and ticked as soon as the couple completes them in their portal, opened with their personal link.

allQuotes.title: Your quotes
allQuotes.body: All your quotes and invoices, with their status. At the top, the year's three figures: signed, invoiced (less credit notes) and collected (less cancellations, earnest money included). A quote is created from its event's page; deposit and balance invoices from the signed quote. « Settings » leads to numbering, the catalogue and document appearance.

faq.q: Why can't I create a quote here?
faq.a: A quote always belongs to an event: create it from the event page, where it stays linked.

adminAccounts.title: Accounts and support
adminAccounts.body: To unblock someone in a team: see whether their two-factor authentication is set up, whether their account is locked and when they last logged in. "Reset two-factor authentication" is for a lost phone; "Resend invitation" sends a new link. Every action is logged.

faq.q: Someone forgot their password?
faq.a: They change it themselves, with "Forgot password" on the login screen.

adminActivity.title: Organisation activity
adminActivity.body: Usage statistics: accounts, accounts active over 30 days, last login, the number of events, quotes and invoices created each month, and the latest storage reading (number of files and size). Never a name, an amount, a file name or any content; guided trials are not counted.

adminClosures.title: Closed workspaces
adminClosures.body: The trace of each workspace closing: organisation identifier, closing date, deletion date, and what was erased (counts). Never a name or any workspace data. Before restoring a backup, export this trace; afterwards, replay it (restore runbook).

forgotPassword.title: Forgot password
forgotPassword.body: Enter your account email: a link valid for 30 minutes is sent so you can choose a new password. The message is the same whether or not the address has an account. Your two-factor authentication stays as it is.

adminOnboarding.title: Organisations getting started
adminOnboarding.body: For each team account: tutorials completed and in progress, and the latest help activity. Enough to spot who needs a hand, without any event data.

vendorBook.title: The vendor book
vendorBook.body: Each supplier has a single record, reused from one event to the next. Filter by family with the top chips, then by type, tag, or around a place. A row opens its record on the right; « Archive » removes it from the book after confirmation. The “Rating” filter keeps only vendors rated at least that many stars.

faq.q: How do I compare several quotes for a line?
faq.a: From an event's budget line, add the vendors you consulted, note their quotes, then pick one.

faq.q: A vendor is missing from the map?
faq.a: Their address was not recognised: complete it on their record.

faq.q: Where do I create a vendor type or family?
faq.a: In Settings › Vendor types: create your families and types, rename them, put each type in its family, with the fields specific to it.

faq.q: Two types mean the same thing: how do I bring them together?
faq.a: Open one of them in Settings › Vendor types, then “Merge with another type”: its vendors and own fields join the kept type.

adminOrganizations.title: Organisations
adminOrganizations.body: All organisations in a table: subscribed modules, team accounts, getting started and last login, 20 per page, with a search by name. A row opens its panel: enable or disable its modules (a disabled module is hidden or "unavailable" to the organisation, never an error), see its accounts and getting-started progress. "New organisation" creates it and invites its owner.

faq.q: An organisation did not get its invitation?
faq.a: Resend it from Accounts: a new link is sent and the old one is disabled.

importTypes.title: The file's types
importTypes.body: Each type in the file is sorted into a family: linked to a type in your vendor book, to a starter type created once for all its synonyms, or left “to sort”. Change what a label becomes, or create it in the family of your choice.

eventTypes.title: Event types
eventTypes.body: Each event has a type: wedding, seminar, birthday… The type says who your clients are, the couple or a client, and the event page, the schedule and the client space follow its wording. Rename a type, choose who its clients are, add more; a type that has events can only be deleted by handing them to another type. Each change is saved when you leave the field; “Undo the last change” takes it back.

quotesDocuments.title: Documents
quotesDocuments.body: The look of your quotes, invoices and credit notes: logo, colour, font, texts and IBAN. The preview updates as you adjust. A document already issued keeps its look; your settings apply to the next ones.

faq.q: Why do headings look darker than my colour?
faq.a: A colour that is too light would be unreadable on white: headings use a darker shade of it.

privacyCase.title: Request case
privacyCase.body: The case guides you to the reply: 1 record, 2 find the data (pre-filled search), 3 erase, export or correct, 4 reply to the person with the ready-to-copy template, 5 close. The legal deadline stays at the top of the case.

faq.q: Why can't I close the request?
faq.a: A request closes once the action is done and the reply is marked as sent: the case lists what is missing.

faq.q: Does the name of the person stay after closing?
faq.a: Yes, as proof of handling, for the set period (5 years by default, Settings tab). The monthly purge then offers to replace it with “[anonymised]”; the type, dates and log of the request stay.

eventsSources.title: Sources and reasons
eventsSources.body: Two lists that help you follow your business. Sources tell where a prospect comes from (Instagram, word of mouth, a fair…): you pick one when creating it. Loss or cancellation reasons explain why an event does not go ahead: you pick one when cancelling it (« Cancel the event… »). Add, rename or remove lines to match the way you work.

faq.q: Does removing a source change my prospects?
faq.a: No: existing prospects keep their source; it is simply no longer offered for new ones.

followUps.title: Prospect follow-ups
followUps.body: Past these delays, the home screen lists under « To handle » the quotes sent and still unsigned, and the prospects you have not heard from. Shorten them if you follow up quickly, lengthen them if your clients take their time.

vendorTypes.title: Supplier families and types
vendorTypes.body: Each supplier has a type (caterer, florist, venue…), filed in a family that gives its colour on the map. Rename a type, merge two duplicates, move it to another family. Open a type to set its fields (capacity, price, hours…) and choose which ones serve as filters in the book.

faq.q: What happens to the records of a deleted type?
faq.a: Before deleting, you choose the type to move them to, or « to sort ». To keep the type's fields, merge it instead.

vendorTags.title: Tags
vendorTags.body: Tags to describe and find your vendors: a style, a facility, a capacity. Symbola suggests some, sorted by vendor family; your imported tags sort themselves in one click (families, tiers). Add one at the top of the page, put it in a group and choose its families. A “tier” group (capacity, surface…) accepts only one tag per vendor.

vendorTravel.title: Travel estimate
vendorTravel.body: When you look for suppliers around a place, the book estimates each trip's distance and duration: straight-line distance times a detour factor, divided by an average speed. It is deliberately approximate, but instant and free. The example updates as you change a value.

vendorDetail.title: Supplier record
vendorDetail.body: The record gathers everything you know about the vendor: contact details, trades and the features of each, rating, indicative prices, history with you. A vendor can offer several trades (photographer and videographer): tick them all; the primary one sets the colour and icon on the map, and the record is found under each of them. “Edit the record” opens it in a large window, section by section; “Next” saves and moves on. Documents (insurance, registration) have an end of validity and can be requested from the vendor. The IBAN is encrypted and only shown masked: if it changes, a banner asks you to call the vendor on the number you already know, never the one in the message announcing the change, before any payment. A note marked confidential is encrypted and reserved for you and the account owner. For a venue, its constraints (music end, vendor access, capacity) check the event program, without ever blocking anything.

faq.q: Does archiving erase its history?
faq.a: No: the record leaves the book, but its services stay on your events and budgets.

vendorNew.title: New supplier
vendorNew.body: A name is enough to create the record; its trades and the rest are filled in section by section, now or later. A vendor can have several trades. The address you enter places the supplier on the map, and you can move the point by hand.

search.title: Search
search.body: The top bar searches your whole organisation: events and clients, quotes and invoices, tasks and help pages. Type a name, a quote number or a word like « VAT ». The ⌘K shortcut (Ctrl K on PC) puts the cursor in it from any screen.

tutorials.title: Tutorials
tutorials.body: Tutorials to follow in the suggested order: each one guides you on the real screen, with a fictitious example you can delete at the end. The menu counter shows your progress; a started tutorial can be resumed from here.

setup.title: Getting started
setup.body: Five questions, one per screen: your business, your event types, your VAT status, your number of events per year and the tools Symbola replaces. Each question has a suggested answer: "Skip" keeps it. Your answers pick the templates loaded (budget lines, planning, programme, catalogue); everything can be changed later in Settings.

setupReady.title: Your workspace is ready
setupReady.body: What Symbola prepared from your answers: event types, planning, budget lines, VAT status. Then two paths: create your first event (clients' first names, date, type: the planning and the budget appear straight away), or explore a fictional wedding labelled "Example", which contacts no one and disappears on its own after 30 days.

activityLog.title: Activity log
activityLog.body: Every sensitive action leaves an entry here that nobody can change or delete: sign-ins, access rights, exports, sharing, invoices, payments and deletions. Any access to your data by the Symbola team appears too, with its reason. Filter by period, type or person.

ledgerArchive.title: Accounting archive
ledgerArchive.body: Each invoice, credit note and payment is chained to the previous one by a fingerprint, and each invoice is kept as issued. Download a year's entries for your accountant, find the originals, and check that nothing has been changed. Symbola also checks the chain every night.

team.title: Team
team.body: The accounts of your organization: you, the owner, and your planners. "Invite" sends a link valid for seven days, single use: the planner joins your organization and can use every module; the team, the activity log, GDPR and settings stay with you. "Remove access" closes their sessions right away, on all their devices; their work stays in the organization. Invitations and removals go to the activity log.

linkPreview.title: “View as” preview
linkPreview.body: This page shows exactly what the person with this link sees: the same sections, the same figures. Nothing can be changed here and nothing is recorded on their link.

dayOf.title: Day-of
dayOf.body: The day of the event on one dark screen, readable in the sun: “Now” (the current item, in large type, with a call to its vendors) and “Next”, worked out on the phone, even without a network. The bottom bar, within thumb reach, calls the contact of the current item and leads to the schedule, the contacts (emergencies, day-of contacts, vendors, couple: call or text in one tap) and the chosen documents. “Keep on this device” copies the screen to the phone: it then opens without a network, and updates each time it is opened with a network. The day is checked in: "Started", "Finished"; a delay offers to shift the rest and notify vendors after your confirmation; "Incident" logs a dictated fact in ten seconds; checklists tick in one tap and the day's payment handovers are recorded. Everything starts from the phone, even offline.

faq.q: How do I open the day without a network?
faq.a: The day before, with a network, open the screen from the “Day-of” button on the event and tap “Keep on this device”. On the day, without a network, open Symbola: the “Offline” page lists the days kept.

faq.q: How do I install Symbola on my phone?
faq.a: iPhone: in Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”. Android: in Chrome, open the ⋮ menu, then “Install app”.

faq.q: When is the copy erased?
faq.a: At midnight the day after the event, when you log out on this device, when another account logs in on it, or with “Remove from this device”. It is not erased when your session expires: the day prepared the evening before stays readable in the morning.

faq.q: What if I lose my phone?
faq.a: “Sign out all my other devices”, from another device, closes its session but cannot reach a phone without a network: the copy stays readable there until the day after the event. Keep your phone locked with a code.

faq.q: How do I keep the seating plan for the day?
faq.a: Add it to the “Documents” tab of the event (PDF or image), then, on the day-of screen, open “Choose the documents to keep” and tick it. Signed quotes, budget documents and quotes from booked vendors can be chosen there too; bank details, never.

faq.q: Where do I add the venue manager or a taxi?
faq.a: In the event's “Schedule” tab, “Day-of contacts” section: name, role and phone. They appear in the day-of directory, below the emergency numbers.

faq.q: How do I check in a sequence?
faq.a: On "Now" (or in the day's schedule), tap "Started", then "Finished". The time is your phone's, even offline. If two people check in the same sequence, both check-ins are kept and the screen shows the first time.

faq.q: What happens when a sequence runs late?
faq.a: If it starts or finishes later than planned, the screen offers to shift the rest of the key moment: by the delay observed (editable), all following sequences by default (untick fixed ones, like a coach arrival), and the vendors concerned. Nothing is sent without your confirmation. Once confirmed, the schedule is shifted, a new version is published and each vendor concerned receives an email; offline, it is sent when the network is back, only once.

faq.q: How do I log an incident in a few seconds?
faq.a: Tap "Incident" in the bottom bar: the field opens with the keyboard; tap its microphone to dictate. Severity and photo are optional; "Save" records the time. Write the facts without guest names; a guest feeling unwell is logged without their name (no health data).

faq.q: Are photos shared?
faq.a: No: incident, checklist and receipt photos stay within your organisation, never shown to clients or vendors. Photograph things rather than people. Reduced on the phone, they are checked on arrival (type, size, antivirus); a refused photo is flagged and the incident stays. They are deleted with the event documents.

faq.q: What happens without network?
faq.a: Everything you do (check-in, shift, incident, box, handover, photo) is kept on the phone and sent in order as soon as the network is back, with the screen open. "3 actions waiting" then "Up to date" tell you. If your session has expired, nothing is lost: sign in again and sending resumes.

faq.q: How do I record a handover on the day?
faq.a: In the budget, mark the instalment "To hand over on the day" (cheque, cash, envelope) with the person handing it over. On the day, the "Payments handed over today" list shows it: tap "Handed over" (and "Receipt" to photograph the receipt). The instalment becomes handed over and paid in the client's budget. Cash: cash payments are capped by law; check the limit that applies before planning a cash handover.

faq.q: Where is the report?
faq.a: The day after the event's last day, in its time zone, the report is ready on the event page (Overview): planned and actual sequences, shifts, incidents and photos, unticked boxes, handovers. It exports as a PDF and stays internal to your team.

offline.title: Offline
offline.body: Without a network, only the days kept on this device open. The other screens come back with the network.

quotesTemplates.title: Quote templates
quotesTemplates.body: One template per event type: sections, lines, options, standard schedule and deposit or earnest money. "New quote" on the event page starts from the template of its type; editing a template afterwards changes no quote already created, which keeps the version it came from. The starter template is to adapt: prices, terms, schedule.

contractTemplates.title: Contract templates
contractTemplates.body: One template per event type: a title and ordered clauses, each mandatory or optional, with variables in braces and a legal role (pre-contractual information, withdrawal, deposit…). When generating, Symbola fills the variables from the quote, the event and your organisation, and names whatever is missing. Every change increases the version; contracts already generated keep their text. The starter template is a starting point to adapt, to be reviewed by a legal professional: enter the date of the last review.

signup.title: Create your workspace
signup.body: Your email address is all we need: the link you receive creates your account and your organization, then opens the setup. No password to choose; you can add one, or a passkey, later.

organizationExport.title: Export my data
organizationExport.body: Download all your business data, free of charge and at any time: a ZIP archive with your data in JSON and CSV, the schema of each table and your documents. The export is prepared in the background; an e-mail lets you know when it is ready. Only secrets (link tokens, sessions), sign-in credentials, trial data and Symbola's operating data are not exported. Reserved for the account Owner.

faq.q: How long does the archive stay available?
faq.a: For the time shown on the screen, then it is deleted. You can prepare a new export whenever you want.

faq.q: Can I open the archive in a spreadsheet?
faq.a: Yes: each table has its CSV file (semicolon separator, UTF-8). The JSON files are the reference: they keep the links between tables.

organizationImport.title: Restore a Symbola export
organizationImport.body: Upload a Symbola export archive to find all your data in this workspace: to change workspace, or to come back after closing one. Only the account Owner can restore, and only into an empty workspace. Symbola checks the archive (format, fingerprints, tables, documents) before writing: a failure writes nothing. Your invoices, credit notes and payments stay read-only records; their chain is verified then extended, and numbering continues. The summary says what is left to do: invite your team, recreate personal links.

organizationClosure.title: Close the workspace
organizationClosure.body: The Owner closes the workspace, with two-factor authentication and the workspace name to confirm. For 30 days, the workspace can only be exported and reopened: the team loses its screens, third-party links close, no e-mail is sent. One e-mail confirms the closing, another warns seven days before deletion. On day 30, everything is deleted, documents included; only a trace without personal data remains at Symbola.

contactsList.title: Contacts
contactsList.body: Each person exists only once in your space: a couple who comes back for a second event keeps their record, details and history. Search by name, address or phone; an email address belongs to one contact only. A household links people (a couple, a family); a company, its contact persons, with its SIREN and VAT number. “Add a contact” opens a blank record in a panel; “Import contacts” brings in your file (CSV or Excel). Trial contacts do not appear here.

contactDetail.title: Contact record
contactDetail.body: The details on the record are the ones used by their events, personal links and quotes: "Edit the record" opens them in a panel, and changing them there changes them everywhere. The history gathers their events, quotes and invoices, and the documents of their events; notes are for the team. "Create an event" picks them as the client straight away. On a household or company record, add the people who belong to it, with their role; a person's record shows which households and companies they belong to. A company's SIREN or SIRET and VAT number carry over to its quotes.

importRows.title: Setting rows aside
importRows.body: A contacts file often mixes clients, prospects and vendors. Choose a column (a category, a type) and tick the values to set aside: those rows are not imported and stay in the gaps report, which you can download. Nothing is saved yet: you can change this choice.

storage.title: Storage
storage.body: On the first of each month, Symbola takes a reading of your business's files, by kind: legal originals (issued invoices and credit notes), signed documents (signed quotes and contracts, evidence files), uploads (event documents, attachments, vendor quotes, vendor book files) and images (logo, uploaded images). Each reading gives the number of files and their size; it is kept month after month. Exports, which are temporary, and guided trials are not counted. Reserved for the account Owner.

emailTemplates.title: Email templates
emailTemplates.body: Who sends the messages to your clients and vendors: by default, you, from your own mailbox. Symbola prepares each relationship message (proposal, reminders, brief, schedule, reply to a prospect…) in the “Prepare the email” window: “Open in my mailbox”, “Copy the message”, then “I've sent it”, which notes the sending in the event's activity. No attachment: the space link is in the message, or download the PDF. Automations leave a “To send” item in “Today”. With “Symbola sends them for me”, messages are sent by Symbola, with attachments and automatic reminders. Technical messages (access, signature, online appointments, security, notices) are always sent by Symbola. The templates below are used either way, in French and English according to each person's language: an unknown variable is refused, and the link cannot be missing. The preview shows the email with sample data; “Send me a test” sends it to your own address only. An email with a variable that has no value is not sent: Symbola tells you which one. “Back to the starter text” erases your version. Each template with a button has its own label, in your own words (“Discover your proposal”); guest templates can be edited too. Font, footer, sender name and signatures: “E-mail branding and signature”.

messageTemplates.title: Message templates
messageTemplates.body: Your standard messages to clients (reply to a first enquiry, meeting suggestion…), for all events or for one type. On the record, “Write to the client” offers the event type's templates, fills in their variables from the record, shows the preview and recipients, then opens your mailbox: you review and send yourself. Each change makes a version: earlier ones can be read and restored.

calendar.title: My calendar
calendar.body: A secret address subscribes your calendar to your dated events, and another, from the record, to an event's schedule. Your calendar refreshes on its own. The address is shown only once; a new address replaces the old one, and removing an address stops it at once.

trash.title: Trash
trash.body: What you delete stays here for 30 days: an event with all its content, a contact, a document, a template. "Restore" puts it back as it was. After 30 days it is erased for good, files included; only the account owner can erase it sooner, after ticking “I understand that … can't be recovered”. Items on a record (task, line, sequence, note…) do not come here: they can be undone for ten seconds after you delete them.

guests.title: Guests
guests.body: The event's guest list, by household: for each, a name and a way to reach them (an adult's email or phone); a child only has a first name and an age range. First set the closing date for replies and the questions, then send the invitations: the check screen shows the list and the reminder schedule. Each adult gets their personal link; for a guest without email, hand out a link to copy or a QR code. Replies come in per key moment. Diets are recorded only with the guest's consent; you see numbers, and only the owner sees names. Everything is erased after the event, with notice.

faq.q: Why can't I enter a guest's diet?
faq.a: Diets and allergies are health data: only the guest gives them, with their consent, on their reply page (or the parent for their child). A diet column in an imported file is ignored.

faq.q: Does a reminder go to a household that replied?
faq.a: No: the reply is checked again just before each sending. A household without an email address appears under “To follow up by hand”.

faq.q: When is guest data erased?
faq.a: Diets 7 days after the last day of the event, the rest 30 days after (privacy settings). You are notified seven days before; one justified postponement is possible.

dietaryOptions.title: Diets and allergies
dietaryOptions.body: The closed list your guests tick, after their consent, on their reply page: common diets and the fourteen allergens that must be declared. Hide a useless entry, or add one with a short label. No religious diet is offered by default: it reveals a religious belief.

portalGuests.title: Your guests
portalGuests.body: Add your guests by household, or import your spreadsheet: duplicates are flagged before anything is saved. For a guest without email, get their personal link or QR code and send it by text. You follow replies per moment; diets show as numbers, never by name.

seatingPlan.title: Seating plan
seatingPlan.body: One plan per key moment with tables (dinner, brunch). Add tables in series (“12 round tables of 10”), or copy the plan of another key moment. Seat a guest or a whole household with the “Move” button, from the keyboard or by touch, or drag them with the mouse. Only attending guests and those who have not answered can be seated; guests not seated stay visible with their number. “Together” and “apart” constraints and overfull tables are flagged, never blocked.

faq.q: A guest declines after being seated: what happens?
faq.a: They leave their table at once and an alert tells you on the plan; clear it once you have seen it.

faq.q: Does the client see the plan or the constraints?
faq.a: No. The plan is built by the team; constraints never leave it, neither to the client nor in a summary.

catererSummary.title: Send the summary to the caterer
catererSummary.body: From the seating plan, “Caterer summary” gives the PDF or the spreadsheet: covers and meals by type, diets and allergens, by table; vendor meals and guests awaiting an answer apart. The owner gets the named version; a team member, the version without names, exact per table. Nothing is kept in Symbola: the copy you send leaves Symbola, ask the caterer to delete it after the event.

mealTypes.title: Meal types
mealTypes.body: The meal types of the caterer summary: adult, child, baby (no meal), vendor to start with. Rename, hide or add a type; a guest's type follows their age, unless you change it on the seating plan. Each change is saved when you leave the field; “Undo the last change” takes it back.

appointmentsList.title: Appointments
appointmentsList.body: Appointments booked on your booking page, and those entered by the team (phone, fair). New, moved or cancelled ones also show in “Today”. Start by creating an appointment type (a name and a duration), then choose your page address and give it to your future clients. Nobody needs an account: each person gets a confirmation with the invitation for their calendar, and a link to reschedule or cancel.

appointmentDetail.title: An appointment
appointmentDetail.body: Move or cancel the appointment: the person is told by email if you tick the box. With the Events module, link it to an event, or create an option from it with nothing to type again. After the appointment, write the report (team only) and its actions: “Make it a task” puts the action in the event's planning, with its due date and owner.

appointmentNew.title: Enter an appointment
appointmentNew.body: For an appointment agreed by phone or in person: choose the type, the day and time (Paris time), then the person. Their contact card is created, or found by their email address. Tick “Notify” to send them the confirmation and their management link.

appointmentSettings.title: Types and booking page
appointmentSettings.body: A type is created with its name and duration; everything else has a default value (video call, 24 hours' notice, bookable 60 days ahead, reminder 24 hours before). The page address is yours (/reserver/your-name); changing it stops the old one. The privacy notice is shown under the form, in your name.

appointmentType.title: Type settings
appointmentType.body: The appointment (name, duration, host, place, description shown on your page), when it can be booked (buffers before and after, notice, horizon, reminder) and the questions asked beforehand. Questions are asked one at a time after the slot is chosen; “Edit” opens a question in place, choices are added one by one, and “Required” prevents booking without an answer. By default, no appointment is offered during your events' busy times (Settings › Busy times).

appointmentAvailability.title: My availability
appointmentAvailability.body: My week: one row per day; the switch opens or closes the day, “+ Range” adds a second range, “Copy Monday to open days” copies Monday; a single “Save”. Then your closed days and calendars: connect your Google, Apple or Outlook calendar by its secret iCal address; only busy hours are read, every fifteen minutes, never the content. If a calendar can no longer be read, no slot is offered until it is read again.

eventsPipeline.title: Follow your requests in columns
eventsPipeline.body: Each card is an event with the Option status, placed at its stage. To move a card, drag it with the mouse, or use its “Move” button and choose the stage (with the keyboard as with a finger). Dropping on “Won” confirms the event once you agree; on “Lost”, cancels it with its reason. In a column, the card that has been waiting the longest is at the top. On a phone, choose the stage in the tabs.

faq.q: Does a stage change the event's status?
faq.a: No: stages are only markers within the Option status. Only “Won” and “Lost” change the status (Confirmed, Cancelled).

faq.q: What is a request “to check”?
faq.a: A contact form request whose message contains several links: it may come from a robot. Accept it to create the prospect, or delete it. Without action, it is deleted after 30 days.

eventsPipelineStages.title: Pipeline stages
eventsPipelineStages.body: Rename stages, add some (ten at most), change their order, remove those you do not use. A stage holding cards is emptied first: choose the stage they move to. Each change is saved when you leave the field; “Undo the last change” takes it back.

faq.q: Can I add “Won” as a stage?
faq.a: No need: “Won” and “Lost” are always at the end of the pipeline; they confirm or cancel the event.

eventsContactForm.title: Put the form on your website
eventsContactForm.body: Open the form, choose its address and give the address of your privacy policy (required). Share the link, or copy the code into your website after declaring its address under “Websites allowed”: the form only shows on those websites. Each request creates a prospect with the Option status, at the first stage of the pipeline, and appears in “Today”. The person receives no automatic email: the reply comes from you.

faq.q: What about spam?
faq.a: The form protects itself without a captcha: an invisible trap field, a minimum filling time, a limited number of submissions. A request whose message contains several links is set aside “to check” in the pipeline.

faq.q: A person you already know fills in the form?
faq.a: They are found by their email, and their record is not changed: what they wrote goes into the request.

followUpReview.title: Review a follow-up
followUpReview.body: The follow-up is ready: review and edit the text, then send it with one click, or withdraw it. Just before sending, Symbola checks again that nothing stops it (reply recorded, stage change, confirmation, refusal, action by the contact).

faq.q: Does Symbola read my emails to know whether the couple has replied?
faq.a: No. When the couple replies (email, phone, WhatsApp), click "Has replied": pending follow-ups stop.

eventQuestionnaires.title: Event questionnaires
eventQuestionnaires.body: Send a questionnaire to a client: they receive it with their personal link, answer at their own pace, each answer is saved. When they finish, empty fields of the record are filled; if an answer contradicts the record, you choose.

faq.q: Is a question already asked asked again?
faq.a: No: a question already answered (in this questionnaire or another) is not asked again; a question whose answer the record already knows is offered pre-filled, to confirm.

questionnaireTemplates.title: Your questionnaires
questionnaireTemplates.body: Create your questionnaires or start from Symbola's (discovery, ceremony, music, practical details). A question can fill an event field (date, guests, budget, venue, town, style, type). Each save of the questions makes a version; questionnaires already sent keep theirs.

faq.q: Can I ask about dietary requirements?
faq.a: Use the Guests module: it collects each person's consent. A question about health, religion or opinions gets a warning.

contactDuplicates.title: Possible duplicates
contactDuplicates.body: Symbola spots records with the same email address or the same phone number, when you enter them and every night. Compare and merge them, or say "these are not the same": nothing is merged without you.

contactMerge.title: Merge two records
contactMerge.body: Choose the record kept then, field by field, the value to keep. The absorbed record disappears; its history (events, notes, messages, appointments, links, signatures) moves to the record kept. The merge is recorded in the log.

portalQuestionnaires.title: Your questionnaires
portalQuestionnaires.body: Answer at your own pace: each answer is saved at once, you can stop and come back later. Click "Finish" when you are done.

vendorCoordination.title: Request quotes from several suppliers
vendorCoordination.body: Write the brief for the category (the need, the number of guests, an indicative budget you show or not, the deadline, some inspiration), tick the suppliers, check the list, then send: each one gets their own email and link, with no account, and never sees the others. Those who have not answered get a reminder the day before the deadline. Answers arrive in the comparison; then tick the proposals to show the client and ask them to choose. Their choice books the supplier, sets the others aside and creates the follow-up tasks. You change the booked supplier whenever you want.

vendorScenarios.title: Compare option scenarios
vendorScenarios.body: A scenario picks at most one supplier per category. Compare two scenarios side by side: categories in rows, totals to the cent, differences highlighted, against the client's envelope and the estimated budget. A quote without an amount counts as “to be specified”. Show a scenario to the client: its suppliers appear in their options.

vendorCoordinationSettings.title: Supplier run sheets
vendorCoordinationSettings.body: Set the default deadline of a brief, the reminder the day before, the run sheets sent 30 and 7 days before to booked suppliers (each confirms with one tap), the delay after which an unconfirmed run sheet is flagged to you, and the follow-up tasks created when the client chooses a supplier.

dayChecklists.title: Event-day checklists
dayChecklists.body: Your organisation's checklist templates (setup, teardown), copied at first from a few standard lists. Add a checklist to a key moment from the event-day screen ("Prepare the checklists"): it is copied, and editing the template afterwards does not change it. “Edit” opens a template in its row; each change is saved when you leave the field.

programImport.title: Import a schedule
programImport.body: A schedule kept in a spreadsheet (CSV or XLSX) imports into the event schedule: columns day or key moment, start, end, sequence, location, responsible, note. The review screen shows the sequences read and the issues row by row; nothing is written before "Import". Missing key moments are created; a cell starting with =, +, - or @ stays text.

settlement.title: Pay the deposit
settlement.body: Payment is made by bank transfer, from your bank: copy the IBAN and the reference, or read the QR code with your banking app. Once the transfer is made, press “I have made the transfer”; your planner will confirm its receipt. No card and no payment goes through this page.

cashCalendar.title: Cash-out calendar
cashCalendar.body: Month by month, what remains to be paid: to your planner and to your vendors, with who pays each instalment and where it stands (upcoming, reported, paid).

portalPayers.title: What each payer sees
portalPayers.body: Your families or a company are contributing? For each of them, choose whether they see only their share (the amount that falls to them and their instalments) or the whole budget.

proposalTemplates.title: Proposal templates
proposalTemplates.body: The page your client receives when you send a quote: your welcome note, your presentation, the quote and its options, the schedule, the validity, then “Accept and sign”. One template for all events, and one per type if needed; each quote reuses the welcome note and can change it before sending.

reminderSettings.title: Quote and payment reminders
reminderSettings.body: When Symbola reminds your clients: a few days before a proposal expires, then after an unpaid instalment. Each reminder goes out once, stops as soon as the client reports their transfer, and can be suspended on the quote.

proposalPreview.title: Proposal preview
proposalPreview.body: The exact page your client sees, without saving anything: check the welcome note, options and amounts before notifying them.

budgetPayers.title: Payers and split
budgetPayers.body: The couple pay for everything by default. Add a family or a company, then split each line by percentage or amount: totals add up to the cent. Choose who pays each instalment, and what each payer sees (only their share, by default).

budgetCashCalendar.title: Cash-out calendar
budgetCashCalendar.body: Month by month, the client's instalments to you and to their vendors, with their payer and status: the answer to “what do we have to pay in May?”.

vendorDocuments.title: Vendor documents
vendorDocuments.body: Insurance certificate, company registration, venue plan: each record in the book keeps its documents with their end of validity. Symbola warns you a few days before (set the delay here) and flags, on the event and in "Today", a document that expires before the big day of a retained vendor. You can also request a document from the vendor: they upload it through their personal link, and it arrives "to check".

plannerMoney.title: Fees and commissions
plannerMoney.body: Set your fees (flat, percentage of the estimated or committed budget, or both): they go on your quote and stay separate from the client's budget. Record the commissions and business referrals paid by vendors: an individual client sees them all, on the quote and in their portal; for a business, you choose. A commission is invoiced to the vendor, in your invoice series, as Factur-X.

sessions.title: My sessions
sessions.body: Each line is a device where your account is signed in, with its last activity (updated at most once an hour). Close a session you don't recognize: it is refused at its next request. Lost a phone? “Close the other sessions”.

accounting.title: Accountant access
accounting.body: The Owner gave you read-only access: invoices (commission invoices to vendors included), credit notes, payments, ledgers, exports and e-reporting. You see neither events, nor guests, nor settings. Two-step verification is asked at every sign-in.

eventTeam.title: Event team
eventTeam.body: Name a lead planner (who receives the event's alerts and digests) and assistants. When “All Planners see all events” is off (Settings, Team), a Planner only sees the events of her team. A big day helper comes without an account: their link only opens this event's Big day mode, from the day before to the day after.

ownership.title: Ownership transfer
ownership.body: The Owner offers to hand over to you. Sign in with your two-step verification, then confirm: the roles are swapped and you both get an email. The link is valid for seven days and works once.

notMe.title: This wasn't me
notMe.body: Your account was signed in from a device Symbola did not know. If it wasn't you, close all your sessions here, then change your address, password and two-step verification in your account.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: What happened and what is waiting for you, one line per fact. Click a notification: it opens the screen where you can act and becomes “read”.

notificationSettings.title: My notification settings
notificationSettings.body: Turn a kind off on one channel without touching the others. The summary is sent every morning at the chosen time; during quiet hours nothing rings, except day-of alerts on the day of an event if you keep that option.

dayReminder.title: Day-of reminder
dayReminder.body: Tick who receives the day-of reminder: you (ticked by default), booked vendors, the event's team and its helpers, the clients. For each, the day before or the same morning, and the time, in the event's time zone. Symbola sends it, with your branding, once per person; never for a cancelled, postponed, trial or undated event. On an event's page (Schedule tab), the reminder can be turned off or given another time for that event only. The four templates are adapted in Email templates.

automations.title: Automations
automations.body: Each row is an automation: what it does, its switch, its send time and its log. The default send time applies to every automation without its own; the email goes out at that time (within five minutes), in the event's time zone, and never at night. Appointment reminders keep their delay (24 h, 2 h before). Turning one off stops its next sends; nothing is caught up when it is turned back on. The GDPR purge and the document check cannot be turned off.

riskRadar.title: Risk radar
riskRadar.body: The radar runs every morning. Each rule has a threshold in days; an alert states the rule that triggered it and leads to the screen where you can act. Planning health is set here too.

clientTerms.title: Client terms
clientTerms.body: The term chosen for a type replaces “the couple” or “the clients” where Symbola names your clients, and slips into your e-mails and future documents. Each change is saved when you leave the field; “Undo the last change” takes it back.

eventClosing.title: Event closing
eventClosing.body: From the day after the event, the closing checklist gathers what is left: the balance invoice, vendor payments, commissions, vendor evaluations (internal), your three lessons and the thank-you to the client with your review link. The review shows the final budget, your fees, commissions, own expenses and margin. Time spent is optional. Close, then archive: the event becomes read-only and leaves your lists.

eventTemplatesList.title: Event templates
eventTemplatesList.body: An event saved as a template keeps its timeline, programme, budget structure (without amounts), questionnaires and, if you chose so, its vendors. Never any client data: Symbola refuses a template that contains some. Create an event from a template by choosing its date.

closingDashboard.title: Your reviews
closingDashboard.body: The closed events for which you entered the time spent, with the margin and the margin per hour. Without time entered, nothing appears: it is optional.

accountingExports.title: Accounting exports
accountingExports.body: Choose the period (month, quarter, year or financial year). Symbola suggests the format from your legal form: receipts journal for a micro-business; sales and payments journals and FEC for a company or a sole trader under the real regime; original PDFs in a ZIP archive. Each export is checked: totals to the cent, continuous numbering including credit notes; a discrepancy blocks the export and is explained. Trial data is never included.

floorplanVenue.title: A venue's floor plans
floorplanVenue.body: Note the venue's spaces once (ballroom, garden, marquee), their size and their fixed installations (sockets, water, exits, delivery access). Then prepare your named layouts, "Dinner for 120, round tables" or "Standing cocktail": they are the starting point of each event's plan in this venue. They belong to you and are never shared with the venue.

floorplanSpace.title: Space, background plan and installations
floorplanSpace.body: Upload the venue's plan as an image (PNG, JPEG or WebP), then calibrate it: two points whose distance you know, and the plan is to scale. Place the fixed installations in the editor: each socket has its number and amperage. They appear in every layout of the space.

floorplanEditor.title: Plan editor
floorplanEditor.body: Place tables and set-ups from the library, then drag, rotate and resize them with the mouse or a finger, snapping to a 50 cm grid.
