With the keyboard: Tab moves from one element to the next, arrows move by 10 cm (1 m with Shift), R rotates by 15°, Delete removes. The properties panel and the list of elements do everything without the drawing, including on a phone. Overlaps, elements outside the space, missing seats and overloaded sockets are flagged, never blocked. Nothing is written before "Save".

faq.q: Does Symbola check the electrical installation?
faq.a: No. The "Power" table helps you spot who plugs in where and flags an overloaded socket based on what you declared. Have the connections checked by the venue or an electrician.

faq.q: Does the floor plan seat the guests?
faq.a: No. It sets up the venue; guests are seated in the seating plan, where you can copy this plan's tables once.

floorplanEvent.title: Event floor plan
floorplanEvent.body: Copy a venue layout into the event and adjust it: the venue does not change. Place the booked vendors, note their needs and link them to a socket. Then share the plan: the client reads it in their "Floor plan" section (closed by default), each vendor sees it through their link with their spot highlighted. Each shared version has a number, flagged to vendors.

floorplanLibrary.title: Element library
floorplanLibrary.body: The tables of every shape and the evening set-ups offered in the editor. Hide what you don't use, add your own elements and set their default size, suggested seats and needs.

floorplanShared.title: Floor plan
floorplanShared.body: The latest version of the plan shared by the planner. Your spot is highlighted, with your needs and your socket; delivery access and exits are shown. The PDF prints to scale. For any question, contact the planner.

subscription.title: My subscription
subscription.body: Your plan, its apps and options, the total and your storage against the plan's quota. Changing plan takes effect immediately; the prorated difference goes on the next invoice. Cancelling takes two steps: “Cancel subscription”, then “Confirm cancellation”; you keep access until the end of the paid period, then the space is closed (export for 30 days, then deletion). At 80% and 95% of the quota, Symbola warns you; when full, new uploads are only refused after seven days' notice, and viewing and export always remain available. Account holder only.

apps.title: All modules
apps.body: All of Symbola's apps, with their state, what they bring and where to find them once active. During the pilot, “Request activation” tells the Symbola team, who activate the app for you, free of charge: you receive a notification and the app appears in your menu. A request can be cancelled until it is handled. The team only sees your organisation's name and the app requested. After the commercial launch, “Add to my subscription” shows the price, the prorated amount and the new total. Reserved to the Owner.

adminPlans.title: Plans and packages
adminPlans.body: The catalogue of plans (trial, plans, Pilot package) and options: names, modules, users, quota and prices, and the trial and quota rules. The Pilot package never appears in self-service. Subscription billing stays off until the company is created. No business data.

adminFeatureFlags.title: Feature switches
adminFeatureFlags.body: Each new feature has its switch, closed to everyone. Open it first to the pilot so she can test it, then to all organisations. The effect is immediate, without redeployment.

eventMessages.title: Messages by topic
eventMessages.body: One topic per theme, each with its thread. Two writing areas: “Shared message” goes to the people named on the button (clients whose link opens the Messages section, the topic's vendors); “Internal note” stays within the team, on a distinct background, and is never sent.

portalMessages.title: Your messages
portalMessages.body: Find each conversation here by topic, with its attachments, without searching your emails. Reply directly: your message goes to your planner.

senderAddress.title: The sending address
senderAddress.body: Your emails are sent from an address in your name on Symbola's sending domain; the display name is your company's and replies go to your contact address. The Owner can change the start of the address.

emailDeliveries.title: The email log
emailDeliveries.body: Each email sent on behalf of your company, with its status. A bounced email is reported to you by a notification and on the contact's page. The log keeps the subject and status for 13 months, never the content.

busyRanges.title: Busy times
busyRanges.body: For each event type, the hours it takes up: for example a wedding, the same day from 8 AM to 10 PM. These hours are marked “busy” in your subscribed calendar, and your booking page never offers them. On an event page, “Change for this event” sets its own busy time (the day before at 2 PM until the day after at noon, for example); if the event is postponed, the busy time follows. If the event has a team, only its members are blocked. An option does not block, unless you turn on “Options also block my calendar”. Do you take appointments with TidyCal or Calendly? “Add to my calendar”, on the event page, puts the busy time in your main calendar, the one these tools read.

eventDocuments.title: Filing an event's documents
eventDocuments.body: One upload area, at the top of the Documents tab: drag the file (or choose it), then say what it is. A vendor's quote or invoice, with the vendor's name, is linked to its line in “Budget and vendors” and filed in “Vendor quotes” or “Vendor invoices”; a contract goes to “Contracts”; anything else to the chosen folder or “Miscellaneous”. “Move to…” files a document elsewhere; on a computer you can also drag it onto a folder. “My quotes” and “My invoices” are the ones you issue: manage them in “My quotes and invoices”.

taskCategories.title: Task categories
taskCategories.body: Sort your tasks by category: Client, Vendors, Admin, Big day to start with. Rename them, change their colour and order, add some; a deleted category leaves its tasks without a category. Each change is saved when you leave the field; « Undo the last change » takes it back.

emailBranding.title: E-mail branding and signature
emailBranding.body: Your e-mails to clients, vendors and guests carry your logo, the colour of your documents, the font chosen here, your full contact details in the footer (with postcode and city) and a free line. The sender display name replaces the organisation name in “From:”; the address stays on the Symbola domain and replies reach your contact address. Each team member fills in their signature in My account › My signature; here you choose what signatures show, and the signature of automatic e-mails (yours by default). “Sent with Symbola” no longer appears on your e-mails: only Symbola’s own e-mails (account, security, codes, team notices) keep its branding.

mySignature.title: My signature
mySignature.body: Your signature is added at the end of the e-mails you send from Symbola: display name, job title, phone, website, up to four links and an optional small photo. The preview shows the result live; save to apply it. Your organisation chooses the elements shown. An automatic e-mail carries the signature chosen by the account holder. In the “Prepare the e-mail” window, “Add my signature” adds it as text at the end of the message. Your signature is erased if your access to the organisation is removed.

EventVendorsImport.title: Take over the selected vendors (PDF)
EventVendorsImport.hint: The “Export des Prestataires” PDF from your previous software, for this event. Each vendor is found in your directory, or created, then selected on the budget line of their trade. Nothing is written before you agree; amounts do not change.
EventVendorsImport.previewTitle: {count, plural, =0 {No vendor read} one {# vendor read} other {# vendors read}}
EventVendorsImport.headerDifferent: The date in this file is not this event's date. Check that it is the right file.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Each event has its page: status, vendors, planning timeline, programme, quotes and clients, organised in tabs. Let's create a fictional birthday party to go through it.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates "Camille's 40th birthday party", with its budget and starter tasks.

steps.title: Confirm the event
steps.body: Open the example, Summary tab, and set its status to "Confirmed", as when a client agrees.

steps.title: Retain a vendor
steps.body: In the Budget tab, pick a line (the caterer, for example) and enter the retained vendor's name: it becomes “Retained”.

steps.title: Tick a task
steps.body: In the Planning timeline tab, tick a task as done: the event's progress updates.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to follow an event from start to finish. The example will be deleted.

retroplanning-template.keep: Keep the template as a base

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: A planning template lists, once and for all, the tasks of a type of event with their lead time before the day. Applied to an event, it creates every task with its date.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional company retreat and an "Express retreat" template to work from.

steps.title: Look at the template
steps.body: The template appears in Settings › Events › Planning templates: each task has its lead time (90 days before, for example) and who does it.

steps.title: Apply the template
steps.body: Open the example, Planning timeline tab, choose "Express retreat" and click "Apply template": the tasks arrive with their due dates.

steps.title: Move the date
steps.body: In the Summary tab, open "Edit the details" and change the event date: Symbola offers to recompute the due dates. Accept and watch them follow.

steps.title: Keep or delete
steps.body: The example event will be deleted. Do you want to keep "Express retreat" as a base for your own templates?

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: The catalogue lists your services with their price, unit and VAT. A quote is built in a few clicks from the catalogue, without retyping anything.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: Symbola notes your catalogue's current state to recognise the service you are about to add.

steps.title: Add a service
steps.body: Open the catalogue and add a service: a label, a unit and a price are enough.

steps.title: What it is for
steps.body: In every quote, "Add a catalogue item" picks up this service with its price and VAT. Changing the catalogue never changes a quote already sent.

steps.title: Keep or delete
steps.body: Do you keep this service in your catalogue?

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: A quote is written from an event's page, sent, then signed online by your clients. Once signed, it confirms the event.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional wedding and an example quote, already filled with lines and a payment schedule.

steps.title: Get it signed
steps.body: Open the example quote, click "Send the quote" then "Get it signed". During an example no e-mail is sent: the signing links show on the quote.

steps.title: Sign
steps.body: Open a signing link shown on the quote and sign on behalf of each client. The quote becomes "Signed".

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to get a quote signed online. The example will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Once the quote is signed, you invoice each deposit of the schedule, then the balance. Numbering is continuous and an issued invoice never changes (corrections go through a credit note).

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional gala and its example quote, with a payment schedule.

steps.title: Get the quote signed
steps.body: Open the example quote: send it, click "Get it signed", then sign through the links shown.

steps.title: Invoice the deposit
steps.body: On the signed quote, in the schedule, click "Invoice" on the deposit. The example invoice uses a separate numbering: it never uses up your real numbers.

steps.title: Invoice the balance
steps.body: Now invoice the balance: it takes the quote total minus the deposits already invoiced.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to invoice a deposit then the balance. The example will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: The split suggests an estimated amount per line from a total, then the budget compares estimated and committed as vendors are retained.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional christening to simulate a budget for.

steps.title: Simulate the budget
steps.body: Open the example's budget, enter an envelope and a number of guests, choose an allocation model and run the simulation.

steps.title: Enter a committed amount
steps.body: Enter a committed amount on a line: the difference with the estimate shows, in terracotta if over budget.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to simulate and follow a budget. The example will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: The day's programme lists the moments of the event, hour by hour, with the vendors involved. It downloads in two versions: for clients and for vendors.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional wedding with an empty programme.

steps.title: Start from a template
steps.body: Open the example's Day programme tab, choose a programme template and apply it (or add a first line).

steps.title: Download
steps.body: Still in the Programme tab, download the vendors' version: internal notes only appear there, never in the clients' version.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to prepare the day's programme. The example will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Your clients can follow their event's preparation in their own space: their tasks, the programme and the budget, never your internal notes or your other events.

steps.title: Create the example
steps.body: Symbola creates a fictional wedding anniversary, with its tasks.

steps.title: The Clients tab
steps.body: In the Couple tab of the example, you will create a personal link for each client: no account, no password (during an example, no link is sent). You can remove a link at any time.

steps.title: What they see
steps.body: In the planning timeline, "Clients" tasks are the ones they will see and can tick; their ticks appear in your activity feed.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to open your clients' space. The example will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Import brings in your existing data: the PDF event sheets from your current tool, or a table (Excel, CSV or JSON). You check a preview, then confirm. A confirmed import can be undone during the undo period.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: Symbola notes your current imports to recognise the one you are about to start.

steps.title: Start an import
steps.body: Open Import data, download the example sheet (a fictitious PDF) from “Bring over my events”, then choose “Event sheets (PDF, one sheet per event)” and drop it in. Go as far as the preview.

steps.title: Check before confirming
steps.body: The preview shows the event that will be created, with its suggested status, and any rejected sheets with their reason. Nothing is saved until you confirm: as this is a test, abandon the import.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: You know how to bring over your existing events, one or several sheets at a time.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: For one budget line (the caterer of a gala, the venue of a retreat…), you often consult several vendors. Symbola keeps them side by side with their quote and your notes until you select one.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: Symbola creates an example event (a charity gala) and, if you have the vendor book, two example caterers. Everything will be deleted at the end.

steps.title: Consult two vendors
steps.body: In the example's “Caterer” budget line, add two consulted vendors: pick them from your vendor book or simply type their name.

steps.title: Record a quote
steps.body: For one of them, enter the quote amount (or attach the file). You can also add a note, internal or shown to the clients.

steps.title: Retain
steps.body: Click “Retain” on the vendor you choose: it becomes “Retained”, the line is committed at its amount, and the other one stays visible as “Dismissed”.

steps.title: What the clients see
steps.body: Tick “Show to clients” on a vendor: your clients find it in their space with the notes ticked “Clients”, never your internal notes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: The example and its example vendors will be deleted.

steps.title: Understand
steps.body: Your quotes and invoices carry your logo, colour, details and terms. A document already issued keeps its appearance: your settings apply to the next ones.

steps.title: Complete your details
steps.body: In Business and VAT, enter at least your SIRET or contact email, and your VAT number if you have one. They are printed in the header and footer.

steps.title: Upload your logo
steps.body: In Settings › Sales › Documents, upload your logo (PNG or JPEG, 2 MB max). Without a logo, your documents show your business name.

steps.title: Choose the colour and font
steps.body: Pick one of the shades or your own colour, and the Modern or Classic font, then save. A colour that is too light is darkened to stay readable.

steps.title: Review the texts and enter your IBAN
steps.body: Review the quote terms and the payment terms, enter your IBAN, then save. The IBAN is printed on your invoices and under your quotes' payment schedule.

steps.title: Download a sample
steps.body: Download a sample quote or invoice as a PDF: it is what your clients will receive. No number is used up.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Your quotes and invoices now look like you. You will find these settings in Settings › Sales › Documents.

appointment_confirmed.title: Appointment confirmed
appointment_confirmed.description: Sent as soon as an appointment is booked, with the calendar invitation and the link to reschedule or cancel.

appointment_reminder.title: Appointment reminder
appointment_reminder.description: Sent automatically before the appointment, according to the type's reminders.

appointment_rescheduled.title: Appointment moved
appointment_rescheduled.description: Sent when the appointment changes time, with the new invitation.

appointment_cancelled.title: Appointment cancelled
appointment_cancelled.description: Sent when you cancel an appointment, or when the person cancels it.

prospect_form_received.title: New contact request
prospect_form_received.description: Sent to the account owner at each request received through the contact form, without the person's message or contact details.

prospect_reply.title: Reply to a prospect
prospect_reply.description: The text offered by "Reply" when no message template fits; the planner reviews and edits it before sending.

prospect_follow_up.title: Prospect follow-up
prospect_follow_up.description: The text of a follow-up with no message template chosen (Settings, Follow-ups); prepared in "Today", reviewed before sending.

questionnaire_sent.title: Questionnaire sent
questionnaire_sent.description: Sent with a questionnaire to the event's contact: their personal link becomes the "Answer the questionnaire" button.

vendor_brief.title: Quote request to a supplier
vendor_brief.description: Sent to each supplier of the brief, with two buttons: “I am available” and “I am not available”.

vendor_brief_reminder.title: Quote request reminder
vendor_brief_reminder.description: Sent automatically the day before the deadline, to suppliers who have not answered.

vendor_roadmap.title: Supplier run sheet
vendor_roadmap.description: Sent automatically 30 and 7 days before the event to each booked supplier, with their link to confirm.

proposal_sent.title: Proposal sent
proposal_sent.description: Sent to the event's clients when you send the proposal, if they have a space to read it in.

proposal_expiry_reminder.title: Proposal expiring soon
proposal_expiry_reminder.description: Sent automatically a few days before the end of validity of a proposal neither signed nor declined.

payment_details.title: Bank details for the deposit
payment_details.description: Sent automatically on the 8th day of a contract signed off-premises, with the bank details and the transfer reference.

invoice_reminder.title: Unpaid instalment reminder
invoice_reminder.description: Sent automatically after an unpaid instalment, according to your settings; stops as soon as the client declares their transfer.

day_helper_link.title: Big day helper link
day_helper_link.description: Sent when you add a helper to an event: their personal link becomes the “Open the big day” button, valid from the day before to the day after.

ownership_transfer.title: Ownership transfer
ownership_transfer.description: Sent to the Planner you name as the new Owner: the link becomes the “Confirm the transfer” button, valid for seven days.

new_device_login.title: New sign-in
new_device_login.description: Sent to a team member who signs in from an unknown device: the link becomes the “This wasn't me” button, which closes all their sessions.

identity_changed.title: Account changed
identity_changed.description: Sent when the email address, two-step verification or password of an account changes: to the former address when the address changes.

daily_digest.title: Morning summary
daily_digest.description: Sent every morning to each team member who keeps it: what is new and what is waiting. The subject contains no personal data.

notification_alert.title: Immediate alert
notification_alert.description: Sent straight away for an “immediate” notification (declared transfer, signed quote, day-of alert), outside quiet hours. The subject only says the kind.

payment_due_reminder.title: Reminder before the due date
payment_due_reminder.description: Sent to the designated payer (otherwise the signers) a few days before a due date, with the amount, the reference and the bank details; never after a declared transfer.

new_message.title: New message
new_message.description: Sent to a client or a vendor when you write to them about a topic: the topic's name and a link to the thread, never the message itself.

day_reminder_planner.title: Day-of reminder to the planner
day_reminder_planner.description: Sent automatically the day before or the same morning, at the set time: schedule, day's contacts, what is still open, “Open the day of” button. Sent by Symbola.

day_reminder_vendor.title: Day-of reminder to vendors
day_reminder_vendor.description: Sent automatically to booked vendors, if you ticked them: their times, the venue, the on-site contact. Sent by Symbola.

day_reminder_team.title: Day-of reminder to the team
day_reminder_team.description: Sent automatically to the event's team members, if you ticked them: the day's schedule and contacts. Sent by Symbola.

day_reminder_client.title: Day-of reminder to clients
day_reminder_client.description: Sent automatically to the event's clients, if you ticked them: a word from you. Sent by Symbola.

guest_invitation.title: Invitation to reply
guest_invitation.description: To each adult guest: their personal link to say whether they are coming, their meal choices and allergies.

guest_reminder.title: Guest reminder
guest_reminder.description: To guests who have not replied yet, following the reminders set on the event.

quoteTemplates.title: No quote template

messageTemplates.title: No message template

payments.title: No instalment to collect
